units.description: Parse a human duration such as "1h30m" into whole seconds: Ok(seconds), or Err(message) if the text is not a valid duration. A duration is one or more parts written one after another with nothing between them; a part is a number of 1 to 9 ASCII digits (0-9 only) followed by one unit letter: w (604800 seconds), d (86400), h (3600), m (60) or s (1). Letters are lower case only. The units must appear in that order, from largest to smallest, and each unit at most once: "1h30m" and "2d4h" are valid; "30m1h" and "1h1h" are not. There is no sign, no decimal point, no spaces, no "ms", and no normalising: "90m" is valid and means 5400 seconds, "00s" is valid and means 0, "007m" means 420. The empty string, a bare number ("1", "0"), a bare unit ("s") and a number of 10 or more digits are invalid. It must never panic, on any text. The text is bytes (cancho has no string type): anything that is not an ASCII digit or a unit letter is invalid.
tests: fn parse_is(s: &static [byte], want: int) -> [] int { match duration_parse(s) { result.Result::Ok(v) => { if v == want { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }
fn parse_err(s: &static [byte]) -> [] int { match duration_parse(s) { result.Result::Ok(_) => { return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 0; } } }
pub fn test_parse_ok_1() -> [] int { test.assert_eq(parse_is("1h30m", 5400), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_parse_ok_2() -> [] int { test.assert_eq(parse_is("90m", 5400), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_parse_ok_3() -> [] int { test.assert_eq(parse_is("1w1d1h1m1s", 694861), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_parse_ok_4() -> [] int { test.assert_eq(parse_is("00s", 0), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_parse_ok_5() -> [] int { test.assert_eq(parse_is("999999999s", 999999999), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_parse_err_1() -> [] int { test.assert_eq(parse_err(""), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_parse_err_2() -> [] int { test.assert_eq(parse_err("1"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_parse_err_3() -> [] int { test.assert_eq(parse_err("30m1h"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_parse_err_4() -> [] int { test.assert_eq(parse_err("1h1h"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_parse_err_5() -> [] int { test.assert_eq(parse_err("1.5h"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_parse_err_6() -> [] int { test.assert_eq(parse_err("1 h"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_parse_err_7() -> [] int { test.assert_eq(parse_err("1H"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_parse_err_8() -> [] int { test.assert_eq(parse_err("1ms"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_parse_err_9() -> [] int { test.assert_eq(parse_err("1000000000s"), 0); return 0; }

units.signature: fn duration_format[&h](heap: &!h Heap, seconds: int) -> [heap] result.Result[buffer.Buffer, &static [byte]]
units.description: Format whole seconds as text: Ok(text), or Err(message) if seconds is negative. duration_format(0) is Ok("0s"). Otherwise the seconds are split greedily into weeks (604800), days (86400), hours (3600), minutes (60) and seconds, largest first, and every unit that is zero is left out: 90061 seconds is "1d1h1m1s", 1209600 is "2w", 3600 is "1h". Anything of a week or more uses weeks (there are no months or years). The text is a heap-owned Buffer (cancho has no string type); the caller drops it.
tests: fn same_bytes[&a, &b](x: &a [byte], y: &b [byte]) -> [] bool { if len(x) != len(y) { return false; } var i = 0; while i < len(x) { if int_of(x[i]) != int_of(y[i]) { return false; } i = i + 1; } return true; }

fn fmt_is[&h](heap: &!h Heap, n: int, want: &static [byte]) -> [heap] int { match duration_format(heap, n) { result.Result::Ok(b) => { var same = false; borrow b as &x in { same = same_bytes(buffer.bytes(x), want); } buffer.drop(heap, b); if same { return 0; } return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 2; } } }
fn fmt_err[&h](heap: &!h Heap, n: int) -> [heap] int { match duration_format(heap, n) { result.Result::Ok(b) => { buffer.drop(heap, b); return 1; } result.Result::Err(_) => { return 0; } } }
pub fn test_format_ok_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(fmt_is(heap, 90061, "1d1h1m1s"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_format_ok_2[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(fmt_is(heap, 0, "0s"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_format_ok_3[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(fmt_is(heap, 59, "59s"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_format_ok_4[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(fmt_is(heap, 604801, "1w1s"), 0); return 0; }
pub fn test_format_err_1[&h](heap: &!h Heap) -> [heap] int { test.assert_eq(fmt_err(heap, -1), 0); return 0; }
